terrain.difficultyNotes: A three-tier breakdown, so percentExpert is null and the top 32% sits in percentAdvanced. These are the resort's own figures, read from crotchedmtn.com once Vail's web estate came back up; the file previously carried OnTheSnow's 29/33/38, which put a further 6 points into the top grade and made the mountain look harder than the operator claims it is. Either way the percentage flatters it: 32% of 25 trails is eight runs on 1,016 feet of vertical, and a black diamond at a southern New Hampshire hill this size is not a black at Cannon. The number that actually defines this mountain is the 63 inches of natural snow set against 100% snowmaking on 100 acres - which is to say all of it, fed by 100-plus fan guns on 3,800 feet of pipe pumping 6,000 gallons a minute. Crotched is a fully manufactured ski area and it is very good at being one.

pricing.notes: 2026-27 season. Vail prices day tickets dynamically by date and publishes no fixed window rate, so the ticket fields are null rather than estimated. The season pass figure is the full adult (31+) Epic Pass; Vail does not sell an unrestricted Crotched-only pass. Crotched carries unlimited access on the Epic Local Pass too, at $829 for 31+, and for a mountain this size that cheaper tier is the only one that makes sense. crotchedmtn.com's content pages became readable again on 2026-08-25 and this file was rebuilt from them, but its ticket and pass pages redirect to Vail's ecommerce waiting room, which requires JavaScript, so the $1,119 still comes from OnTheSnow's Epic buyer's guide - its current-cost line, not its prose, which quotes the March 2026 on-sale price of $1,089.

editorial.overview: Crotched is one of the smallest mountains on this roster - only Big Rock has less terrain - and it has built a genuine identity out of the one thing bigger mountains cannot be bothered to do: it stays open at night, on all of it. A hundred acres, 25 trails and 1,016 feet of vertical in Bennington, an hour from Boston and forty minutes from Manchester, with night skiing Tuesday through Saturday until 9pm and Midnight Madness on select Saturdays - which the resort calls, plausibly, the latest skiing and riding in the Northeast. OnTheSnow records 100 acres of lit terrain against 100 skiable acres, so this is not a lit trail or two, it is the mountain. That is what Crotched is for, and it fills the hill with a young Boston-and-Manchester crowd on weeknights that gives the place an atmosphere the daytime skiing does not earn on its own. Because with 63 inches of natural snow a year everything you ski here is made - 100% snowmaking coverage, 100-plus fan guns - and 100 acres is a small canvas. The Rocket, southern New Hampshire's only high-speed quad, gets you back up it quickly. Come for a Wednesday night. Do not plan a February Saturday around it.
editorial.snowQuality: Sixty-three inches is a very low natural total - half of what Gunstock gets an hour north and a third of Wildcat's - and it is a straightforward consequence of being in southern New Hampshire at 2,000 feet. Crotched's answer is complete rather than partial: 100% snowmaking coverage on 100 skiable acres, fed by more than a hundred fan guns connected by 3,800 feet of pipe pumping 6,000 gallons of water a minute. Every trail on the mountain is machine-covered, the system is good, and the hill is reliably open, which for a ski area this far south is the whole achievement. What it means for a skier is that the surface is manufactured all season and the freeze-thaw cycles of southern New Hampshire are the thing to watch - a January thaw here is a real event in a way it is not at Sugarloaf.
editorial.crowds: Two different mountains depending on the hour. Daytime weekends draw a Boston and Manchester day-trip crowd onto 100 acres and five lifts, which is not much terrain to spread people over, and it feels full. The night sessions are the interesting half: a younger, more local crowd, more of it in the terrain park than on the trails, and a genuinely good atmosphere on a Tuesday or Wednesday evening. Midnight Madness nights sell the place out in a different way - it becomes an event rather than a ski day, which is either the appeal or the problem depending on what you came for.
editorial.difficulty: Small, and the percentages flatter it. Thirty-two percent of the trails carry the resort's top rating, but 32% of 25 trails is eight runs on 1,016 feet of vertical, and the pitch that earns a black diamond at a southern New Hampshire hill would be a blue at Cannon. There is glade skiing, but on 63 inches of natural snow it opens rarely. What Crotched is honestly good for is a competent skier who wants laps rather than a challenge - five lifts on 100 acres, one of them a high-speed quad, means very short rides and a lot of runs in an evening - and for park riders, who get a real share of the mountain's attention across two properly designed parks. Nobody should drive past Gunstock to ski Crotched's terrain in daylight.

keyTrails.name: The Rocket
keyTrails.note: Southern New Hampshire's only high-speed quad, and the reason an evening here turns into a dozen laps rather than five.

keyTrails.name: CM Park
keyTrails.note: The advanced park and, on a night session, the busiest place on the mountain. A giant A-frame, flat boxes and full block-party set-ups.

keyTrails.name: NCC-1701
keyTrails.note: The medium park - flat-down rails and boxes and medium jumps - and the rung most riders here actually spend their time on. Yes, it is named after the Enterprise.

keyTrails.name: Midnight Madness
keyTrails.note: Not a trail but the reason people come: skiing and riding on select Saturdays long after every other lift in New England has stopped.

reviews.gist: A straightforwardly favourable write-up that rests the case on the night operation — every acre lit, Tuesday through Saturday, with Midnight Madness on selected weekends — and on fan-gun snowmaking that runs without burning fuel. The nearest thing to a criticism is geographic: southern New Hampshire does not hold natural snow for long.

Calls the snowmaking superb and makes the comparison concrete — Crotched open on fourteen or fifteen trails while Mount Sunapee sat on eight. Also notes it is quieter than Vail’s other New Hampshire properties. The caveat is that the black diamonds and the park are pitched at intermediates, so an advanced skier is not the audience.

moguls.policy: A mountain covering 100 of its 100 acres with snowmaking is protecting a manufactured surface, and that means comprehensive grooming - a hundred acres of machine snow left to bump up would be unskiable within a week at southern New Hampshire temperatures. No grooming policy is published; the resort's site, readable again as of this revision, describes its parks and its night operation in detail and says nothing about ungroomed terrain. This remains inference from the snowmaking figure rather than a sourced statement, and it is recorded at the cautious end.
moguls.quality: There is no meaningful bump skiing at Crotched and nothing here pretends otherwise. This is a 100-acre fully manufactured mountain whose freestyle attention goes into its parks and whose distinguishing feature is that the lights stay on. Anyone in southern New Hampshire who wants moguls is looking at Gunstock's Tiger terrain an hour north, or Wildcat if they are willing to drive.

parks.name: CM Park
parks.note: The resort calls it the final stop on the progression train, with every feature designed for riders who have worked up to technical ones - a giant A-frame, flat boxes and full block-party set-ups. Where visiting pros ride.

parks.name: NCC-1701
parks.note: The middle rung: flat-down rails, flat-down boxes and medium jumps, aimed at riders already comfortable on boxes and small jumps. Named after the registry of the starship Enterprise.

parks.progression: Explicitly built as a ladder, which is more than most mountains this size manage, though the bottom rung is missing from the published account: NCC-1701 is described as the step for riders who are already comfortable with boxes, rails and smaller jumps, and CM Park as the final stop after that. Where a true first-timer starts is not stated. Crotched also runs the NSAA Smart Style programme and puts park safety front and centre on the page, which reads as genuine rather than boilerplate for a mountain whose park traffic is this large a share of its business.
parks.overview: Two parks, both named, both described, and the resort's statistics block and its terrain parks page agree on the count - which is worth saying because its sister mountain Mount Sunapee contradicts itself on the same question. CM Park is the advanced end: a giant A-frame, flat boxes and block-party set-ups. NCC-1701 is the medium park, with flat-down rails and boxes and medium jumps. No feature counts, no lighting detail and no rebuild schedule are published, and there is no pipe.
parks.reputation: Crotched is understood locally as a park-and-night mountain rather than a skier's mountain, and the resort does not fight that reading - freestyle gets two of its five named fun facts and a page with more detail on it than the trails get. Two well-defined parks on 100 acres is a serious allocation of a small mountain, and the combination of park riding and lights until 9pm is genuinely hard to find anywhere else within an hour of Boston. What it is not is a destination park on the scale of Carinthia at Mount Snow.
